title: Make vs Zapier
intro: Make and Zapier are two of the best-known no-code automation platforms. Both connect apps so that events in one trigger actions in another, and both have free plans with usage-based paid plans.

The main difference is the building experience: Zapier uses a step-by-step list, while Make uses a visual canvas that shows branching and data flow. Which suits you depends on how complex your workflows are and how you like to work.
similarities: Both are no-code automation platforms that connect web apps.
Both have a free plan and usage-based paid plans.
Both support webhooks and multi-step workflows.
Both offer templates to get started.

differences.a: Visual canvas with modules and routes
Billed by operations/credits — check official definitions
differences.b: Billed by tasks — check official definitions

differences.a: More to learn, but complex logic is easier to see

considerA: Your workflows branch, loop or transform data.
You like seeing the whole workflow visually.
You often call APIs directly with HTTP requests.
considerB: You want the quickest path to simple trigger-action automations.
Non-technical teammates will build and maintain automations.
You rely on apps with less common integrations — check both directories.

faqs.q: Which is cheaper, Make or Zapier?
faqs.a: It depends on how many runs and steps your workflows use, because both price by usage. Estimate your monthly volume and compare current plans on each official pricing page.

faqs.q: Can I move automations from Zapier to Make?
faqs.a: There is no universal one-click migration; workflows usually need to be rebuilt. Plan time to test each workflow after moving.
